in_greek.name: Ἑριβέρθα
in_greek.long_meaning: ὄνομα γυναικὸς μετονομασία της Εὐσεβείας - ἡ Εὐσεβεία ἦταν ἡ ἡμέρα ἡ οποία ἐνταφιαζόταν οἱ ὄψεις τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἔχουν τὴν σοβαρότητα τοῦ ἔργου. data.spiritual_symbolism: Heriberta: derived from Germanic elements, "heri" meaning army or warrior and "berht" meaning bright or famous. This name symbolizes a woman of strength and illumination, radiating courage and brilliance in her actions.

historical_references.reference: Heriberta was the name of the youngest daughter of Count Heribert II of Rhétie and his wife Gertrude of the Conradines. She was born around 1030 and married Otto, Count of Burgundy, in 1054. Heriberta was an important figure in the political landscape of the Holy Roman Empire during the 11th century.
historical_references.context: Early Middle Ages, Holy Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Heriberta, also known as Herberta of Burgundy, was the mother of five children, including the future Holy Roman Emperor Conrad III. She was the daughter of Count Otto-William II of Burgundy and Adelaide of Aquitaine. Heriberta's marriage to Duke Conrad III of Swabia around 1090 was a strategic alliance to strengthen the Hohenstaufen dynasty. Heriberta died in 1114.
